clarity.justification: The goal and method align: the proposal predicts that, "on error trials," the attributed-belief readout will "shift toward the own-belief value," that projecting out the own-belief direction will "reduce errors," and that forcing early commitment will produce "increased leakage/error." These are directional and refutable—absence of the predicted shift, improvement, or increase would count against the respective claims—and the matched cases "where they coincide," true-belief accuracy, and explicit variation of agent access are relevant comparisons. However, the plan leaves the operational definition of "own belief," the probe locations and labels, the leakage metric, and the criterion for concluding that two channels are partially distinct unspecified, with the submission itself acknowledging that defining own belief is "nontrivial and prompt-sensitive"; no numeric decision thresholds resolve these ambiguities.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is to "train probes for own-belief and attributed-belief" and then "subtract the own-belief direction (or project it out)" at an attribution position; linear probing, activation extraction, and subspace projection are standard, well-supported interpretability operations, although selecting the position and identifying a channel-specific direction without probe or representation confounds requires custom engineering rather than a magic step. The required methods exist in standard ML tooling, while the information-asymmetry artifact is to be constructed using the defined divergence and "matched controls where they coincide"; those controls, true-belief accuracy, the reverse intervention, and varying agent access make a negative result runnable. Feasibility is weakened because no model, layer set, dataset size, number of scenarios, probe protocol, or other concrete resource figure is supplied, so an implementer must still choose substantial parts of the experimental design.
